_meta.extraction_method: Google Sites public HTML read on 2026-10-03. Publication/preprint titles, author order, source numbering, status and links reconciled with existing files; suspicious links checked against arXiv/APS/ICML and final published metadata preferred when verified. Exact source text and source links retained per record. Profile/teaching/conference sources separately checked; verified external corrections are recorded.
known_source_anomalies: Preprint 23 (metallic systems) links to arXiv:2608.19797, which is Optimal Sobolev Approximation (preprint 22). Wrong link omitted; correct link unresolved.
Preprint 21 (Autonomous Knowledge Distillation) links to arXiv:2607.19786, which is Structure-Adaptive Random Feature Method (preprint 20). Wrong link omitted; correct link unresolved.

Preprints 11 (Flexible Boundary) and 8 (NanoTitan) link to arXiv:2506.07401, which is A Study on Fine-Tuning U-MLIPs (preprint 6). Wrong links omitted from both unrelated entries; correct links unresolved.
Publication 32 contains an empty whitespace anchor to IADR OpenReview; it is not a link to Configuration Selection. It is intentionally omitted.

Publication 28 links to the APS author-submission dashboard. Replaced with verified public DOI 10.1103/j89c-3k2s. Earlier Symmetry-Protected title consolidated with the accepted Geometry-conditioned title based on strongly matching primary-source abstracts; title continuity is an inference recorded on the publication.
The Tutorial (publication 18) lists a different author sequence on Google Sites; the final AIP author order is used. Yangshuai Wang is corresponding author.
The CPC article (publication 19) uses an earlier title on Google Sites; final publisher title is used, preserving its existing local URL.

The IMA JNA article (publication 2) gives author order Yangshuai Wang, Hao Wang, Lei Zhang and year 2020 on Google Sites. Oxford final version gives Yangshuai Wang, Lei Zhang, Hao Wang, volume 41(2), 2021; online publication was 19 May 2020. Final citation updated; existing URL preserved.
Preprint 7 (AI-ready battery interfaces) is dated 2025 on Google Sites but arXiv first submission is January 2026. The source manuscript year 2025 is retained; no 2025 arXiv-deposit date is claimed.

Three preprints absent from the latest Selected Preprints page are preserved locally as drafts, not described as withdrawn: Stopping Reliability, Geometry of Adapter Placement, Long-Range Operator Learning.
OpenReview IADR and LDD-RFM URLs were preserved from Google Sites; automated fetch reaches a browser-verification page, so public paper metadata was not independently rechecked there.
The incorrect Google Sites mentor hyperlink for Weizhu Bao was replaced with the NUS-confirmed homepage https://blog.nus.edu.sg/matbwz/.
CV page still says updated September 2023 and exposes no downloadable current CV; no current CV PDF was fabricated.

The existing local portrait and Google Scholar link are retained from the repository. No new personal profile links or portrait were invented; the current Google Sites homepage also contains an image.
Teaching source has no course title for MATH 100 (Autumn 2023); course code retained without an invented title.

Only publication_year is retained when the publication date is known to year precision. Synthetic January 1 dates were removed so search metadata cannot mistake them for actual publication dates. The book source has no year and no year is assigned.

profile.bio_intro: My research is situated at the intersection of Numerical Analysis, Scientific Computing, and Computational Materials Science. I focus on developing mathematically rigorous and computationally efficient methods for molecular modeling and multi-scale simulation. My specific research directions include:

items.subtitle: LLMs for Scientific Discovery:
items.text: Investigating the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and specialized foundation models to accelerate scientific workflows, automate property prediction, and facilitate "inverse design" in materials science.

items.subtitle: Scientific & Quantum Machine Learning:
items.text: Developing data-driven solvers and Quantum Machine Learning (QML) techniques for solving high-dimensional PDEs. My work emphasizes the development of robust numerical algorithms with a focus on Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) and the theoretical analysis of convergence and generalization.

items.subtitle: Numerical Analysis of MLIPs:
items.text: Advancing the mathematical foundation of interatomic potentials by investigating approximation errors, stability, and the reliability of force-field predictions.

items.subtitle: Multi-Fidelity & Coarse-Graining:
items.text: Developing systematic approaches for fine-tuning pre-trained models and constructing coarse-grained (CG) force fields for soft-matter systems.

items.subtitle: Applications in Materials:
items.text: Applying these potentials to study complex phenomena in energy storage and conversion materials, ensuring a seamless integration of physics-based priors with data-driven flexibility.

items.subtitle: Coupling Methods:
items.text: Engineering and analyzing Atomistic-to-Continuum (A/C) and Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) coupling schemes.

items.subtitle: Rigorous Error Estimation:
items.text: Implementing both a priori and a posteriori error analysis to guide the development of adaptive algorithms that balance accuracy and computational cost.

items.subtitle: Boundary Conditions:
items.text: Formulating sophisticated boundary conditions to accurately capture the long-range strain fields associated with crystalline defects.

items.subtitle: Data-Driven Microstructure Modeling:
items.text: Utilizing machine learning to decipher the kinetics of microstructure evolution in complex systems, including optical and magnetic materials.

items.subtitle: Multi-scale Property Prediction:
items.text: Intersection of multiscale behavior and surrogate modeling to predict macroscopic material performance from mesoscopic morphological data, facilitating the accelerated design of high-performance materials.
